Engineering notes: `MachineSetupModal` hardcoded the install panel for Claude Code only. Kiro, Kimi and Antigravity rendered a status line and a description; Codex matched no branch and rendered an empty body. The old Connect page's `ToolCard` drove the same panel from each executor's `ToolStatus` (`installId`, `needsSignIn`, `guidance.steps/command/link`), which `connect-status-impl` still produces for every executor. The modal now renders that status for Codex, Kiro, Kimi and Antigravity, reusing `InstallButton` and `SignInButton` from `connect-panel`. Install it for me appears only where `installId` is set, which `isInstallableId` limits to executors with a verified installer (Claude Code, Codex, Kiro); Kimi and Antigravity get the copy command and link, because no installer of theirs has been verified here. Claude Code's own panel is unchanged. Separately, the Codex card fell through `ConnectionCard`'s hand-written `MACHINE_SLUGS` list and rendered no button, so the modal was unreachable for it; the list now derives its executor slugs from a `Record<AiExecutorId, string>`, so a newly registered executor fails `tsc` until its card can open setup. ## v243 (2026-10-18): a second terminal opens beside the first

### What's new for you (fix, v0.96.0)
Opening another terminal now shows it next to the one you already have, instead of hiding it behind a tab.
- When a workspace already has a terminal open, a new assistant or command line switches the view to the grid, so you see both at once.

In Focus layout `openTab` added a tab and made it active, which hid the terminal already open; a double-click on a pane header or its Focus button switches to Focus and remembers it, after which every new terminal behaved that way. `layoutAfterOpen` (`lib/terminal/grid-layout.ts`) now returns `grid` when the workspace already has a terminal, and `openTab` applies and remembers it. ## v244 (2026-10-19): brain memory map

### What's new for you (feature, v0.96.0)
The brain page now opens on a map of what your AI knows about your company.
- Every fact and note is a dot, joined to the things it links to, so you can see at a glance what your AI has to work with.
- Dots show what it always knows, what it can look up when it needs to, and what it is unsure about.
- Filter the map by kind, or search to find a dot by name.
- Click a dot to see what it says and what it links to.
- Open the full note to read it with its links and the notes around it.
- When your AI is unsure about a fact, you can confirm it with the assistant from the same panel.
- The plain list is one click away if you prefer it.

Why: the brain page showed a list and an agent graph, which said little about what the AI actually knows. The design is in the brain memory map spec: show the company's own memory, the way an Obsidian vault shows its notes, and make the unsure parts easy to settle.

Engineering notes: `lib/os/brain/` holds the data side. `company-facts.ts` and `memory-links.ts` read the facts and the links between files; `memory-graph.ts` builds nodes and edges (always known, look-up, unsure); `memory-graph-read.ts` reads files from git, committed content only, so an uncommitted edit never shows up as something the AI knows. The result is cached per HEAD, with a bounded number of concurrent git reads, so a large company folder does not spawn hundreds of processes and an unchanged HEAD costs nothing. `app/api/brain/note/route.ts` serves one note to the note view: read-only, the path is checked to stay inside the company folder and to be a tracked file, anything else is refused. `components/os/brain/memory-map.tsx` (with `memory-map-state.ts` for the pure filter, search and selection logic) is the map; `memory-note-view.tsx` is the note view with links and a local map of neighbours. The map's colours are variables scoped to the map in `globals.css`, with values for both themes, so light and dark stay readable without touching the shared palette. The brain page now defaults to the map and `brain-view-switch` keeps the list one click away. The old graph components (`knowledge-graph.tsx` and friends) are left in place, unused by the default view, for a later cleanup.

Live result: a production build was checked against the real Alacrán company. The counts (4 always known, 184 look-up, 2 unsure), the type filters, the side panel, the note view and Esc back to the map all worked. That check found no fit-to-view, a hairball of about 190 overlapping labels, a hydration warning, and a hint sitting over the dots, so a fix wave followed. The canvas is now measured so screen and map units match (drag and zoom track the cursor). The layout is computed once, off screen, with no settling animation. The map fits itself to what is shown, searched for or focused, and pans a picked node into view. Labels show only for folders, always-known, unsure and skill dots, the dot in focus and its neighbours, and search matches, with the rest appearing once zoomed in. Folder children cluster tightly. The map stays mounted under an open note, so Esc returns to the same view. The svg is not drawn until the canvas is measured, so the server render has nothing to mismatch. Hardening: the note route refuses glob characters and ends git's argv with `--`, and the loader passes `--no-optional-locks` and degrades to an empty graph instead of a 500. The hub table moved to `memory-hubs.ts`, so the yaml parser leaves the client bundle. Known gaps: "Confirm this fact" with the ElevenLabs voice dock opens the voice dock without the prompt. Untracked company skills still show as nodes. The old map components are no longer reachable and await a cleanup slice.

## v245 (2026-10-19): remove the old brain map

No user-facing change, so no What's New block. v244 made the memory map the brain page's default and left the previous map stack in place; nothing imported it any more. This slice deletes it: 12 components under `components/os/brain/` (the knowledge, neural and lifecycle graphs, graph canvas and tabs, definitions tree, review rail and their detail panels), 15 modules under `lib/os/brain/` (the old view-model adapter, knowledge-graph builder, layouts, lens, lifecycle, personnel and SOP playbooks, memory-core, memory-search and helpers), their 12 test files, and the 205 lines of CSS only they used (`.brain-layout`, `.brain-graph*`, `.brain-lifecycle*`, `.brain-tree*`, `.brain-review-rail*`, `.kg-halo`). About 9,200 lines in all.

Orphans were found by walking the import graph of `app/`, `components/` and `lib/` repeatedly until no new file dropped out, counting only non-test importers; CSS classes were checked with `/usr/bin/grep -w` across `app`, `components`, `lib` and `landing`. Kept on purpose: `lib/os/brain/canonical.ts`, which the org-chart tests (`components/os/org/org.test.ts`, `lib/os/org/hierarchy.test.ts`) use as fixtures, and `.brain-page`, `.brain-tabs`, `.brain-tab` and `.brain-empty`, which the brain page, the department shell and the tasks board still use. `tsc` clean, 461 test files / 4,189 tests pass, lint has no errors (warnings fell from 27 to 16 with the deleted files), `npm run build` passes.

## v246 (2026-10-22): a living brain map, full page, and confirm by voice

### What's new for you (feature, v0.97.0)
The brain map now feels alive, and you can open it full page.
- Dots drift gently, the things your AI always knows glow and breathe, and sparks run along the links like neurons firing.
- The whole map sits in one round cloud.
- "Full page" fills the window with the map; Esc or "Exit full page" brings you back.
- "Confirm this fact" now hands its question to the voice assistant too, instead of opening it with nothing to say.
- With your Mac's "Reduce motion" setting on, the map stays still.

Why: the owner found the map static and asked for dots that pulse and drift "like neurons firing" (the firing version was picked over a calmer breathing one from live mockups), in a round shape (a round cloud, picked over a wheel of rings), with a full-page view. The ElevenLabs gap was a known v244 gap.

Engineering notes: `components/os/brain/memory-map-motion.ts` is the motion. `useAliveMotion` runs one requestAnimationFrame loop that writes straight to the svg elements `MapCanvas` marks with `data-node` and `data-edge` (each dot drifts at most `DRIFT` = 4 graph units around its laid-out spot on a rhythm keyed off its id, and links follow), so React does not re-render every frame. Sparks are circles added to a `data-sparks` layer, about two or three a second, eased along a random drawn link; the dot they reach gets a CSS flare that removes itself. The loop is off under `prefers-reduced-motion`, while a note covers the map, and until the canvas is measured. Halo breathing and the unsure flicker are CSS (`.mm-breathe`, `.mm-flicker`) inside a `no-preference` media query. The layout adds a `round` force that pulls anything past `60 + 24·√n` back in, and a faint radial glow marks the cloud. Full page is a state on `MemoryMap` that makes its wrapper `fixed inset-0` above the assistant dock (z 55); the canvas is keyed on it, so it remounts, measures the new box and refits. Esc steps back note, then selection, then full page; "Confirm this fact" leaves full page so the dock is not hidden. `AssistantDock` now passes `initialPrompt` to `AgentStage`, which sends it once as typed text a tick after mount, the same way `AssistantStage` does; that wakes the voice agent, which the click asked for.

Live result: checked on an isolated dev server (fresh worktree, scratch data dir, built-ins off, a stub `claude` that skipped headless runs; none fired) against a copy of the Alacrán company. Dots move, sparks and flares appear, full page fills and frames the map, Esc and Confirm both leave it, and Confirm opens the dock with the fact's question. That check found the map not refitting in full page and white sparks invisible on the light theme; both were fixed. Not checked live: the ElevenLabs voice path itself, which needs a configured agent and spends minutes.

## v247 (2026-10-22): readable map labels and notes with brackets in their names

### What's new for you (fix, v0.97.1)
Names on the brain map stay readable, and every note can be opened.
- When you pick a dot on a zoomed-out map, its name and its neighbours' names are now easy to read instead of tiny.
- Notes with a star, a question mark or a square bracket in their names (like "[draft] plan") now open like any other note.

Why: both were known gaps from v244.

Engineering notes: labels were drawn at a fixed 10 map units, so at the minimum zoom (0.3) they were 3 pixels on screen. `labelSize(k, strong)` in `memory-map-state.ts` keeps them at least 9 screen pixels, 11 for the dot in focus and its neighbours, and 10 map units once zoomed in; the label sits `1.3 × size` below its dot, and a stroke in `--bg` painted under the fill (`paint-order: stroke`) keeps an enlarged label legible over other dots. Which labels show is unchanged (`shouldLabel`). The note route (`app/api/brain/note/route.ts`) refused `*`, `?` and `[` as glob characters, but its git call is `git show HEAD:./<path> --`: an object name after the colon is read literally and no pathspec follows the `--`. Checked on a real repo: `[draft] x.md`, `what?.md` and `a*b.md` open, while `notes/*.md` and `notes/a?b.md` are "bad revision" rather than a match. The route now allows them and passes `--literal-pathspecs`, so a pathspec added later stays literal too. Control characters, absolute paths, `..`, leading dashes and backslashes are still refused before git runs.

Live result: checked on an isolated dev server (fresh worktree, scratch data dir, built-ins off, stub `claude`; no headless runs fired) against a copy of the Alacrán company with a `notes/[draft] plan.md` added. At zoom 0.3 a selected dot's label measured 11 screen pixels (was 3). The `[draft]` note opened from "Open the full note", and `notes/*.md` through the route returned not found.

## v248 (2026-10-26): held steps wait for your OK

### What's new for you (feature)
An unattended job can now ask before it sends, pays or changes access, and keep going while it waits.
- When a job reaches a one-off message, a payment or an access change, it is held in Approvals under "Unattended jobs need you" instead of being done.
- Each held step says what kind it is, which job asked, and for a message the full recipient, subject and text.
- Approve a held message and Alacrán sends exactly that message once. Reject it and nothing is sent.
- Approving a payment or an access change records your yes; Alacrán can't do those itself, so you do the step. It stays in Approvals, saying so, until you press "Done, clear it".
- If a message fails to send, its card says why. When the job still wants to send it, it offers it again on its next run.
- With several waiting, approve or reject them all at once. Approving all first tells you how many messages go to how many people.
- A practice run only shows what it would have held; nothing from it can be approved.
- Each job's page keeps a history of what you approved, sent, rejected or what failed to send.

Why: the gate in AGENTS.md §6 was a rule the agent was trusted to follow. For unattended jobs it is now enforced by the app: a job can only ask, and only the owner's decision in the app moves a step forward. It also unblocks one-off sends that no pre-approved send policy covers. Inspired by Cloudflare OS Gatekeepers (`notes/company/cloudflare-os-comparison-2026-10-26.md`, item 1).

Engineering notes: the job report (`lib/jobs/runner.ts` `ReportSchema`) gains an optional `hold` array, at most 50 entries of `{row: publication|money|credentials, title ≤300, detail ≤2000, mail?: {to, subject ≤300, body ≤20000}}`. A `superRefine` uses the send lane's exported `EMAIL` regex, refuses a leading dash in subject or body, a multi-line subject, and a `mail` on a money or credentials row; one bad entry rejects the whole report, as a bad `send` does. The queue is `<data>/jobs/<company>/held.json`, beside `approvals.json` and outside the company folder. `jobStore.readHeld`/`updateHeld` read it strictly (only a missing file is empty), so a corrupt file is reported and never overwritten with `[]`. `lib/jobs/held.ts`: `recordHolds` dedupes on a hash of job, row, title, detail and mail against items still pending or sending; `decideHeld` claims items `pending → sending` under the store's per-path lock, sends outside it through the existing `outlookSend` (which adds `--confirm`), then records `sent` or `failed` under the lock again, so a mail goes out at most once and a failure is never retried. Rejecting a failed item, an approved Money/Credentials item ("Done, clear it") or an item stuck in `sending` past the 60 s send timeout (`SEND_TIMEOUT_MS`, `lib/jobs/held-words.ts`) sets `clearedAt` and leaves it in history. Approved Money/Credentials items stay open in Approvals and count in the badge until cleared, since the owner still owes the step; history pruning (newest 500) never drops an open item. Only the phase-1 claim can fail with "nothing was changed or sent": a failed phase-3 record is counted per item, the rest still send, and the owner is told a message may have gone and to check Outlook's Sent folder. A failed send stores Outlook's reason without the CLI's "or run: ..." terminal hint; a new hold of the same step clears the old failure, so a re-hold replaces it. A held mail's `to` must be printable ASCII, and zero-width or bidi control characters (U+200B-U+200F, U+202A-U+202E, U+2060-U+2069, U+FEFF) are refused in title, detail, subject and body, so what Approvals shows is what is sent. The "Unattended jobs need you" section now lives in `HeldActionList`, always mounted, so a decision's result survives the refresh that empties the queue. Phone fix found on the way (pre-existing): at <=640px the closed assistant dock (`aside.os-dock`, z-index 50) was still 100vw wide and swallowed every tap on the page; the full-width rule now applies only to `.os-dock[data-open="true"]`. The sweep holds only from a live run that didn't fail; a practice run writes `would-hold` into its `RunEntry.holds` and nothing to the queue. The server actions `approveHeldAction`/`rejectHeldAction` take the exact ids the owner was shown (UUID-checked, at most 200), never "everything pending now". `openFlagCount` now adds open held steps, so all three Approvals badge sums (`lib/os/pending-approvals.ts`, `app/layout.tsx`, `app/c/[companyId]/layout.tsx`) agree by construction; an unreadable queue counts 0 and the Approvals page says it can't be read. Held steps show in both modes, like the v240 flags, because the section is already in use and counted in the badge. No network call is added beyond the existing Outlook send on approval.

Left open for the owner: whether held steps should expire; whether one-off mails should respect a company-wide do-not-contact list; whether scheduled AI runs (Kimi, Codex and Google Antigravity don't enforce tool scope) should also write held steps; whether a later job run should read Money and Credentials decisions. A crash between "sending" and "sent" leaves the item at "Sending…", never retried; once past the send timeout the owner can clear it after checking Outlook's Sent folder.

Not yet run live: a real Outlook send on approval of a held mail. Tested only with a stand-in sender; the owner's live check (approve one held mail to their own address) is still owed.
